class.name: CharacterMovementComponent2D
class.brief_description: Walking, falling and jumping for a 2D pawn.
class.description: The 3D component's twin, and deliberately a twin rather than a shared base: Godot keeps 2D and 3D in separate hierarchies all the way down, and GFGD already follows that with [PlayerStart2D] and [PlayerStart3D]. What [i]is[/i] shared is everything with no dimension in it. [MovementState], [MovementInput], [ProposedMove], [FloorResult] and [MovementMode] are the same classes as in 3D; a 2D state keeps its position in the x and y of a [Vector3] and leaves z alone. That way there is one set of types, one mode contract and one prediction story rather than two. [b]Units are pixels[/b], and the defaults are Unreal's centimetre values unchanged - which is what the usual "a metre is a hundred pixels" convention makes them. The 3D component divides the same numbers by a hundred. [b]Up is negative Y.[/b] Godot's 2D screen axis points down, so [member up_direction] defaults to [code](0, -1)[/code]. Not in the 2D component yet: crouching, swimming, flying, moving platforms, layered moves and transitions. Those are 3D only for now.

method.name: add_custom_input_flags
method.description: Sets bits of [member MovementInput.custom_flags] on the next tick's input - sixteen bits the game gives its own meaning. They come back out through [signal custom_input_flags], [i]inside[/i] that tick, on every machine that runs it: the client that predicted it, the server that received it, and every replay of it. That is how an action that changes movement is predicted. Queue the dash from the signal, not from the button: done from the button it starts on the client at once and on the server whenever the action state happens to arrive, and the two disagree by the difference. [codeblock] const FLAG_DASH := 1 << 0 func _on_dash_pressed() -> void: movement.add_custom_input_flags(FLAG_DASH) func _on_custom_input_flags(flags: int) -> void: # connected to custom_input_flags if flags & FLAG_DASH: movement.queue_layered_move(make_dash()) [/codeblock] Bits set between two ticks are OR-ed together and cleared once a tick has used them, the same way [method jump] is latched.

method.name: client_receive_move_ack
method.description: Remote call, from the server to the owning client of a predicted character: every move up to [param frame] has been simulated, and [param packed_state] is where that left the character. Sent by [PredictedMovementBackend]; not for game code.

method.name: find_water_volume_at
method.description: The [WaterVolume2D] covering [param point], or [code]null[/code]. The 2D equivalent of [method CharacterMovementComponent.find_water_volume_at].

method.name: get_immersion_depth_at
method.description: How much of the capsule the water is holding up at [param from], from [code]0.0[/code] (dry) to [code]1.0[/code] (head under). The 2D equivalent of [method CharacterMovementComponent.get_immersion_depth_at].

method.name: get_movement_backend
method.description: The [MovementBackend] driving this component: a [PredictedMovementBackend] when [member client_prediction] was on at [code]_ready[/code], otherwise a [StandaloneMovementBackend]. Its counters are what to look at when prediction misbehaves.

method.name: get_velocity
method.description: Current velocity in pixels per second.

method.name: is_replaying
method.description: True while a predicting client is replaying moves after a correction. Every signal this component emits - [signal movement_mode_changed], [signal crouch_changed], [signal layered_move_started], [signal custom_input_flags] - fires again for a replayed tick, so a listener that must react once, such as a sound or a particle, checks this first. A listener that changes the simulation - queuing a layered move - must [i]not[/i] check it, or the replay will differ from the original.

method.name: rollback_to_state
method.description: Makes [param state] the present: the [MovementState], the body's transform, the capsule's size and the cached floor all move together, and the floor is looked for again from the restored position. What a prediction backend calls before replaying. The movement base is dropped rather than restored - it is a snapshot of where a platform [i]was[/i], and no rollback can put a platform back - and found again on the next tick.

method.name: server_receive_moves
method.description: Remote call, from the owning client to the server: the client's newest unacknowledged moves, for frames [param first_frame] onward. Dropped unless it comes from the pawn's owner, and every direction is clamped to length 1 on arrival whatever the client sent. Sent by [PredictedMovementBackend]; not for game code.

method.name: simulate_with_input
method.description: Runs one simulation step with an input that was already gathered - a move the server received from a client, or one a predicting client is replaying. Nothing is read from the [Pawn] or from the [method jump], [method crouch] and [method add_custom_input_flags] latches, and the latches are left for the live tick they were set for.

members.member: The owning client simulates its own character immediately instead of waiting a round trip for the server to, and is corrected when the server disagrees. See [PredictedMovementBackend]. Read once, at [code]_ready[/code]. Off, nothing about it costs anything: the backend is a [StandaloneMovementBackend], and there is no history and no remote call. On, it changes three things beyond the backend: the owning client runs this pawn's input bindings too (see [PlayerController]), what the server replicates for this character is dropped on arrival by the owning client, and input that drives movement should be gated with [method Pawn.wants_movement_input] rather than [method Pawn.has_authority]. It only helps where the simulation is the same on both machines. Anything that changes movement from outside the tick - a layered move queued from a button, a velocity set from a script - happens on one side only and is corrected; send it through [method add_custom_input_flags] instead.
Half the capsule's height while crouching, in pixels. The 2D equivalent of [member CharacterMovementComponent.crouched_half_height].
Downward acceleration along [member up_direction], in pixels per second squared. Defaults to 980, which is Godot's own 2D default.
Upward speed applied on [method jump], in pixels per second.
How hard the character accelerates towards [member max_walk_speed], in pixels per second squared.
The speed flying accelerates towards, in pixels per second.
The tallest obstacle that may be stepped onto rather than blocked by, in pixels. See [member CharacterMovementComponent.max_step_height] for how the climb is decided.
The speed swimming accelerates towards, in pixels per second.
The speed walking accelerates towards, in pixels per second.
The speed walking accelerates towards while crouched, in pixels per second.

Carries the character along with whatever it is standing on. There is no [code]rotate_with_base[/code] twin here: the 2D component writes only a position back to the body, so there is no character rotation for a platform to turn.
The push a jump gives while swimming, in pixels per second. Taking it hands over to [code]Falling[/code] in the same tick - see [member CharacterMovementComponent.out_of_water_jump_velocity] for why.

How far, in pixels, a prediction may be from the server's answer before it is corrected. Too tight and the character twitches on every packet; too loose and a real disagreement is left standing. An exact simulation disagrees by nothing at all, so this only has to absorb what is genuinely not predicted.
The same for velocity, in pixels per second.
Which way is up. Defaults to [code](0, -1)[/code], because Godot's 2D screen axis points down - every sign in the solver depends on this being right and nothing else catches it.

signal.name: custom_input_flags
signal.description: Emitted inside a tick whose input carries custom flags - see [method add_custom_input_flags] - before the movement mode runs, so a layered move queued from here starts on this very tick. Fires on the predicting client, on the server, and again on every replay; that is the point.

signal.name: prediction_corrected
signal.description: Emitted on a predicting client when the server disagreed with its prediction for [param acked_frame] by more than the tolerance. The character has already been moved to the server's answer and [param replayed_ticks] moves replayed on top of it; [param position_error] is how far off the prediction was. One now and then is the server doing its job - a respawn, a hit. A steady stream means something in the simulation is not the same on both machines.
